ANIMATED PREVIEW
THE PROJECT

What it is and why it exists

A net-worth ledger that aggregates assets and liabilities into one live number, with on-demand refresh and a dated history. It is the same discipline as commission and financial reporting work — one number, computed from entries a human can audit — with the arithmetic done in code rather than by a model.

Highlights

  • Aggregated live net-worth total
  • Manual + web-search-driven balance refresh
  • Auditable history
HOW IT WORKS

The mechanism end to end

No hand-waving: this is the actual chain, in the order it runs.

01

Accounts as entries

Each asset and liability is a row with a value and a date; there is no hidden cell arithmetic.

02

Refresh deliberately

A balance updates by hand, or by a web-search job that looks up a published value and proposes it.

03

Append, never overwrite

Every change is a dated entry, so a wrong number is visible in the trend instead of silently replacing the old one.

04

Compute in code

Totals are a query over rows. A language model never does the arithmetic.

BUILD IT YOURSELF

The steps in order, with the traps

This is the short version of what I would do again — including the parts that bit me first.

01

Store facts, compute totals

Never let a model do arithmetic you can do in SQL.

02

Append-only history

If a value can be overwritten silently, you cannot trust the trend.

03

Make refresh explicit

A button, not a background job, for numbers that matter.

WHAT I LEARNED

Notes from the build

NOTE 02The valuable part of finance automation is the audit trail, not the total.
